body:
m1 - TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN NUMBERS, and one real bug found while making them.

CORRECTION 1. I said "of the EIGHT paraphrases that declare a source target, ONE is hit at top-5". IT IS SEVEN, not eight. There are 10 paraphrases and THREE declare Vector.empty targets - RoleSwappedFoil, NegatedFoil and ExternalAssociation - not one as I said. I got eight by splitting the source file on a string rather than counting at runtime, which over-counted the declarations by one and under-counted the empties by two.

So the corrected headline: OF THE SEVEN PARAPHRASES DECLARING A SOURCE TARGET, ONE IS HIT AT TOP-5 OUT OF THE BOX. The finding is unchanged in substance and my denominator was wrong. I also mis-stated which cases are empty-target, which matters because RoleSwappedFoil and NegatedFoil are FOILS - they are supposed to anchor as Distorted rather than to a plain target - so counting them as ordinary misses was wrong twice over.

CORRECTION 2, and this one is more useful: I NOW HAVE THE DECOMPOSITION, which changes what the out-of-box number means.

  defaults                              top5 1/7   mean source mass 0.267
  externalFloor 1.2 only                top5 2/7   mean source mass 0.466
  suite weights only                    top5 4/7   mean source mass 0.605
  suite weights + floor 1.2, NO SYNONYMS top5 4/7  mean source mass 0.818
  floor 2.0, default weights            top5 4/7   mean source mass 0.988

CALIBRATION ALONE TAKES IT FROM 1/7 TO 4/7, with no synonym table at all. So more than half the out-of-box failure is MISCALIBRATED DEFAULTS, not missing semantics - and notably, simply raising externalFloor to 2.0 with otherwise default weights does as well as the suite's tuned weight vector. That is a much more actionable finding than "the defaults do not work": the defaults are wrong in a way that is cheap to fix, and someone should probably fix them.

But 4/7 is the CEILING across every calibration variant I tried. THE REMAINING THREE NEED SOMETHING CALIBRATION CANNOT PROVIDE. That is where the synonym table earns its place, and it is the honest boundary between "tune the numbers" and "we need graded semantics".

THE BUG, filed as bd-01M171DBN80HMVAKNKEK30GRP9. Touching WarOfTheGhostsExpectations BEFORE WarOfTheGhostsModel makes the model fail validation:

  claims.unique-ids @ claims/wog:claim:member:null:null: 2 claims share id
  entity-relation.membership-acyclic @ entities/null: cyclic membership

Touch the Model first and it loads fine, 71 situations. fixturesJVM is 114/114 green. So the error is a LIE - it reports four specific, entirely fictitious defects in the story model, and anyone writing a consumer that happens to touch Expectations first will be told their model is corrupt. I lost time to exactly that before working out it was ordering. Expectations imports Model.{E, S}; Model never references Expectations; the nulls are the signature of a nested-object initialisation cycle. I have proved the order dependence and matched the signature; I have NOT proved the mechanism and said so on the bead.

METHOD NOTE ON MYSELF: both corrections came from the same habit - I counted by grepping a file instead of asking the runtime, and I dropped inference failures with `.foreach` on an Either instead of matching Left. The second could have hidden a real failure behind a smaller denominator. I have been telling other people all day to measure rather than read; I read.
